canonical_requirement_boundary: The original persisted contract remains authoritative; semantic_contract.py creates a deterministic versioned derived verifier view.

checks.authoritative_requirement_ledger: Requirement ID, original expected fields, scope, classification, authority, tolerance, and provenance remain available to the ledger; canonical fields are additive diagnostics.
checks.revision_persistence: The derived view is deterministic from the persisted requirement and normalization version, so revisions can retain stable requirement identity and recompute without rewriting history.
checks.frontend_display: The semantic-policy result preserves semantic_contract diagnostics, allowing a frontend to show canonical meaning, unsupported qualifiers, and fail-closed status without knowing verifier aliases.
checks.user_revision_reference: Revision instructions can refer to the stable requirement ID and user-facing semantic meaning; they do not need to name wall/value or count/diameter implementation aliases.
checks.diagnostic_explanation: Pass, measured failure, and unverifiable outcomes remain distinguishable; normalization diagnostics explain missing, conflicting, shadowed, and unsupported fields.
checks.application_contract_stability: Canonical fields are policy-scoped and versioned; semantically different fields are not collapsed, and original contract fields are not silently replaced.
